title: Cockpit contract v1
description: Two documents share this file: `state` (written by `hw cockpit-state`, read-only for the mod) and `preflight` (printed by `hw preflight --json`). Timestamps are epoch milliseconds. A field that the schema allows to be null is always present. The writer emits exactly the fields this file names. A reader checks `schema` and reads the fields it uses; it ignores a field it does not know, and treats a file in which a field it uses is missing or of the wrong type as dead.

generated_at.description: Writer clock. The reader compares it with its own clock to classify freshness.

seq.description: Increases by one on every write.

invoker_pane.description: The brainer pane whose executors these rows are.

ok.description: false when the herdr RPC failed: rows is then empty and the totals are zero.

server_started_ms.description: Not provided in v1: always null. The one RPC the writer makes (`pane list`) does not carry it and a second call per beat is not worth a field nothing reads (the mod ignores it). A later schema may fill it without a change of shape.

omitted.description: Executors the writer left out because rows is capped at 64, always the lowest-ranked ones (so a challenge, ask, blocked or report is the last to go). The other counters count listed rows only.

holder.description: Task id holding the cut; null when none.

rows.description: Already in hw's order: the mod never sorts. Order is attention rank (challenge, ask, blocked, report, working, idle, gone), then attention_since ascending (null sorts first, as 0), then id. Beyond 64 the writer drops from the end and counts them in totals.omitted.

pane.description: Executor pane id; the argument of the `ruling` verb.

task_n.description: 1 for the first task of the session, +1 per `hw next`.

vendor.description: The harness as hw recorded it (claude, opencode, codex, pi, …): text as it is, not a closed list; `unknown` when the run recorded none.

effort.description: The run's resolved effort, from the `effort=` line of its dispatch file; null when the run has none (or only the agent's own default). The card shows it beside the model, nothing when null.

agent_status.description: herdr's own status for the pane.

turn_state.description: The `turn_state` token the executor's turn-end adapter published; null before its first turn ends or when the vendor publishes none.

children_running.description: Free text from the adapter, e.g. `2 shell`; null when none.

ctx.description: Context use. pct, tokens and source are all null when the vendor publishes nothing (the row then shows `ctx n/a`); never a guess.

attention.description: `gone` is reserved and not emitted in v1: a row is built from a live herdr pane, so a pane that vanished leaves the list instead of becoming a row. It keeps its place in the order so a later writer can emit it without reshuffling.

summary.description: The done-invoker summary, its token chunks rejoined by the writer. A pointer, not the report.

engram.description: The engram project label done-invoker publishes in its `engram` token. It is NOT a list of observation ids; the ids are inside the summary text.

pending_reply.description: Absolute path of the hold file the executor left for this ask (`pending-reply-<n>` in its task state dir): the argument of the `reply` and `challenge-reply` verbs. A string exactly when the ask is delivered and the hold is valid and addressed to this pane over the herdr route; null otherwise (the mod then draws no reply button). An idle executor holding an ask gets a reply button, not a ruling one.

actions.description: Which buttons are valid. Computed by hw with the predicates the verbs themselves refuse on; the mod renders, it never decides.

verify.description: The mod may pre-fill the verification prompt for the person to send (prompt.fill). It starts no verb, so it is not in verbs.txt.

ruling.description: True only where `hw ruling` would queue the correction: the executor is working or awaiting a child, or it reported --blocked and is kept waiting. An idle executor (including one holding on an ask or challenge) is false: hw refuses it and points at `channel-send --ruling`, which is not an allowlisted verb.

why_not.description: One entry per action that is false, hw's own refusal text. An action that is true has no entry.

preflight.description: `hw preflight --json -- <dispatch argv>` takes the argv of the dispatch WITHOUT its leading `hw` (so `hw demo task-a --brief b.md` is checked as `-- demo task-a --brief b.md`) and prints exactly one of these and exits 0 whatever the level; a non-zero exit or unparsable output means preflight is unavailable (the mod fails open). It has no side effects. `level` is the highest `rules[].level`, `ok` when rules is empty. `block` says hw itself would refuse the dispatch; the mod only displays it (v2 stays warn-only).

id.description: account-override: an explicit --account that differs from the lane default; `block` only where hw's own account resolution would refuse it, otherwise `warn`. cut-running: a suite cut holds the gate; warn, for any dispatch, never block.

x-state-classes.description: How a reader classifies a state file, from generated_at and its own clock. Evaluate in this order; the first that matches wins. See fixtures/index.json for one example of each.
x-state-classes.1-dead: file missing, unparsable, size > 1 MiB, schema != 1, a field the reader uses missing or mistyped, generated_at in the future (age < 0, no tolerance), or age > 60 s: no rows, never the old ones
x-state-classes.2-stale: 15 s < age <= 60 s: rows dimmed, banner, action buttons hidden (also when herdr.ok is false: there are no rows to dim)
x-state-classes.3-herdr-down: age <= 15 s and herdr.ok is false: no rows
x-state-classes.4-fresh: age <= 15 s and herdr.ok is true
